title: Deep learning perturbation models can outperform baselines on calibrated metrics - Nature Biotechnology
gist: Shift Bioscience researchers show that the widely reported failure of deep-learning genetic perturbation models to beat trivial baselines is largely an artifact of miscalibrated metrics (MSE, Pearson delta-ctrl) suffering control bias and signal dilution. Using a positive-control baseline and a new 'dynamic range fraction' calibration score across 14 datasets and 18 metrics, they find models such as PRESAGE, scLambda and CellFlow beat baselines on well-calibrated weighted and rank-based metrics, reframing the viability of in silico target-discovery screens.

insights.claim: Prior benchmarks found that deep-learning genetic perturbation models fail to beat uninformative baselines such as a 'mean baseline', but this paper argues those conclusions stem largely from miscalibrated metrics like MSE and Pearson delta-ctrl that have reduced sensitivity to positive model performance.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Revives the investment case for AI virtual-cell / in silico perturbation platforms that skeptical benchmarks had undercut.
insights.quote: common benchmarking metrics (for example, mean squared error and Pearson Δ) are frequently miscalibrated, with reduced sensitivity to measure positive model performance

insights.claim: Two artifacts let uninformative predictors score well: control bias, where systematic control-versus-perturbed differences inflate control-referenced correlations, and signal dilution, where whole-transcriptome error metrics swamp effects concentrated in a small number of differentially expressed genes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Diligence on perturbation-model claims should check which metrics were used and whether they are prone to these artifacts.
insights.quote: Together, these effects allow uninformative predictors to achieve deceptively high scores even when they fail to capture underlying biology

insights.claim: In the Replogle22 K562 genome-wide Perturb-seq dataset there were only 3.25 differentially expressed genes per perturbation on average versus 102.09 in Norman19, which explains why even a technical-duplicate positive control underperformed the mean baseline on MSE in about 95% of K562 perturbations.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Most genome-scale CRISPR perturbations are weak, so dataset choice heavily shapes apparent model performance.
insights.quote: for Replogle22 K562 GWPS, there were only 3.25 DEGs per perturbation on average (versus 102.09 for Norman19)

insights.claim: SP2 transcription factor knockdown in Replogle22 K562 shows near-zero MSE calibration, yet gene set enrichment recovers SP2's own binding targets among top gene sets, demonstrating real biological signal that MSE fails to register.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence that standard metrics can hide genuine biology in perturbation data.

insights.claim: Under well-calibrated metrics, even earlier models scGPT and GEARS mostly outperform uninformative baselines on Replogle22 K562, implying their perturbation-specific signal was present but obscured by metric choice.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Prior negative press on single-cell foundation models may have understated their utility.
insights.quote: suggesting that their perturbation-specific signal was present but obscured by metric choice

insights.claim: The authors introduce an 'interpolated duplicate' positive control that blends a technical-duplicate prediction with the mean baseline per gene using weights derived from differential-expression P values, yielding consistently positive performance.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Provides a reusable positive control that could become standard in AI-biology benchmarks.
insights.locator: Motivated by this observation, we introduce

insights.claim: The 'dynamic range fraction' (DRF) meta-metric measures what fraction of the gap between a negative control and perfect performance is realized by a positive control, with values near zero signaling a metric unable to detect real improvements.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A general tool to audit whether any benchmark metric can actually discriminate good models, applicable beyond perturbation modeling.
insights.quote: In a miscalibrated scenario, DRF values approach zero, reflecting limited metric sensitivity to detect improvements over the negative control.

insights.claim: Across 18 metrics, weighted and rank-based metrics such as weighted MSE, weighted R-squared delta and normalized inverse rank consistently showed higher calibration than MSE and Pearson delta-ctrl, which were well calibrated only in strong-perturbation datasets like Norman19.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Benchmarks and challenges that adopt weighted/rank metrics will rank models very differently from older leaderboards.

insights.claim: Well-calibrated metrics keep higher calibration even with lower data quality, such as fewer cells, lower sequencing depth, weaker perturbations or lower-variance gene sets.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Robust metrics reduce the data-generation cost needed to evaluate models credibly.
insights.locator: To evaluate the reliability of our calibration

insights.claim: The authors caution that no single well-calibrated metric is definitive: scGPT posts the best weighted MSE and DEG Pearson delta-ctrl on Replogle22 K562 yet scores only 0.081 on Pearson delta-pert across all genes, barely above the mean baseline.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Single-metric marketing claims from AI-bio vendors warrant skepticism; demand multi-family evaluation.
insights.quote: we caution against treating any single well-calibrated metric as definitive
insights.locator: Our results also show that models

insights.claim: Models that rank well on well-calibrated metrics also better recover pathway-level biology, with rank correlations of 0.76 on Replogle22 K562 and 0.84 on Wessels23 between pathway recovery and calibrated-metric rankings.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Calibrated metrics track downstream usefulness for target and pathway discovery.
insights.locator: We also evaluated whether model performance

insights.claim: Newer architectures PRESAGE (prior-knowledge attention), scLambda (variational autoencoder) and CellFlow (flow matching) stand out against baselines, and on every metric at least one deep learning model outperformed all baselines in Replogle22 K562, replicated in Nadig25 HepG2.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Model generations are improving measurably, supporting continued investment in virtual-cell modeling.
insights.quote: on every metric, at least one deep learning model outperforms all baselines

insights.claim: In probes of foundation-model gene embeddings, GenePT and ESM2 embeddings proved more predictive of perturbation responses than Geneformer and scGPT, and results held when probe capacity was cut to a half or quarter.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Text/LLM- and protein-language-model embeddings may beat single-cell foundation models as perturbation representations.

insights.claim: Prior biological knowledge in perturbation representations appears valuable, with PRESAGE notable for its knowledge-based representation and an independent preprint by Cole et al. reaching complementary conclusions.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Curated biological knowledge graphs remain a moat versus pure scale-driven foundation models.
insights.quote: further underscoring the value of prior knowledge for building informative representations of genetic perturbations
insights.locator: In summary, we found that models

insights.claim: Norman19, the most widely used combinatorial benchmark, is saturated by the additive baseline because about 96% of effects are additive and training covers only 31 of 4,950 possible gene pairs (0.63%), so the authors recommend it not be used as the sole combinatorial benchmark.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Claims about learning nonadditive genetic interactions on Norman19 alone should be discounted.
insights.quote: we recommend that future studies refrain from using this dataset as the sole benchmark of combinatorial perturbation modeling

insights.claim: On Wessels23, where training covers 10.3% of possible combinations, multiple models beat the additive baseline and PRESAGE exceeded it on 15 of 18 metrics, showing deep learning can surpass additivity when combinatorial coverage is sufficient.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Combinatorial data coverage, not just model architecture, gates value; data-generation capacity is a key asset.
insights.quote: deep learning models can outperform the additive baseline when combinatorial coverage is sufficient
insights.locator: To test whether models can surpass additivity

insights.claim: Performance differences across datasets largely track task difficulty rather than model-specific failures, with median DEGs of one in Replogle22 K562 and zero in Nadig25 HepG2 versus eight in Wessels23.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cross-dataset comparisons of AI-bio models need normalization for perturbation strength.
insights.locator: Our benchmarking revealed that model performance

insights.claim: The authors argue reliance on uncalibrated benchmarks has been a key obstacle obscuring true model performance and that calibration-aware evaluation establishes a more optimistic foundation for genetic perturbation modeling aimed at scalable in silico screens for therapeutic target discovery.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Supports thesis that AI could compress wet-lab target-discovery costs.
insights.quote: Overall, our findings reframe the debate on the feasibility of genetic perturbation modeling.

insights.claim: The study leaves the unseen-context task, predicting responses in unobserved cell types, donors or conditions, unaddressed, and conclusions are a snapshot of a rapidly evolving field.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Generalization to new cell contexts, the most commercially valuable task, remains unproven.
insights.locator: Several limitations remain for this work

insights.claim: Five of the six authors are employees of Shift Bioscience and another is Chief AI Scientist at Xaira Therapeutics, and the work received no external funding.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Commercial AI-drug-discovery firms have an interest in a pro-model conclusion; findings are peer reviewed and code is public.
